title: Canonical derived ringed-topos adjunction is shift-compatible
statement: Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small ringed sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R_X,R_Y$ and structure map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, and let $L=Lf^*$ and $R=Rf_*$ be the canonical derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] constructed from K-flat [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] with the derived adjunction [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] $L\dashv R$, unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Equip $L$ and $R$ with the canonical integer-shift comparisons in the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] obtained by shifting the chosen K-flat and K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. Then the derived adjunction is compatible with these comparisons in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]: for every integer $n$, the unit and counit commute with shift, and the shift comparison on $R$ is the unique one compatible with the unit and the fixed shift comparison on $L$.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); derived.tex Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact). Canonical comparison from Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); shift/coherence details expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Write $Q_Y,Q_X$ for localization, $v=f^*$ and $u=f_*$ on module sheaves. The module adjunction $v\dashv u$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] supplies its termwise homotopy-category adjunction. Denote its Hom bijection by $T$, so $T(t)=u(t)\circ\eta^0_P$ for $t:vP\to I$. For every integer $n$, $v(P[n])=(vP)[n]$ and $u(I[n])=(uI)[n]$: an additive functor carries $(-1)^n d$ to $(-1)^n$ times the image differential. The degree-$r$ component of the termwise unit at $P[n]$ is $\eta^0_{P^{r+n}}$, the same as that of $\eta^0_P[n]$. Consequently $T(t[n])=T(t)[n]$, including in homotopy classes.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; termwise shift calculation expanded here

proof.text: Shifting preserves the resolution classes. For K-flat $P$ and any acyclic $E$, the map $\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes P[n])\to\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes P)[n]$ multiplies the summand $E^i\otimes P^{j+n}$ by $(-1)^{ni}$. In the first differential the signs agree because $(-1)^{n(i+1)}=(-1)^n(-1)^{ni}$; in the second differential both sides have sign $(-1)^{ni+i+n}$. This is an isomorphism, so the target and source are acyclic simultaneously. The definitions [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] thus give K-flatness of $P[n]$; flatness of its terms is just reindexing. K-injective resolutions shift by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. Since $H^r(C[n])=H^{r+n}(C)$, shifted quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms. Localization commutes with these shifts by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Section 06YL, definition-K-flat; explicit tensor signs; derived.tex Definition 070H and shift convention

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_P:LQ_YP\to Q_XvP$ be the canonical left-derived comparison and $\beta_I:Q_YuI\to RQ_XI$ the right-derived comparison. The first is invertible for K-flat $P$ with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]; the second is invertible for K-injective $I$ by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $\ell_A:L(A[n])\to (LA)[n]$ and $r_B:R(B[n])\to(RB)[n]$ for the comparisons in the item, with $n$ fixed. In the localization/termwise identifications of Steps 1–2 their defining equations on these representatives are
$$\alpha_P[n]\circ\ell_{Q_YP}=\alpha_{P[n]},\qquad r_{Q_XI}\circ\beta_{I[n]}=\beta_I[n].$$
These equations also hold if $P,I$ differ from the chosen resolutions. Indeed, for a chosen resolution $p:P'\to P$, naturality gives $Q_Xv(p)\alpha_{P'}=\alpha_P LQ_Y(p)$; both comparisons and $LQ_Y(p)$ are invertible. Apply this equality to $p[n]$ and cancel the same isomorphisms to obtain the first equation. For $I$, compare the chosen resolution $I\to I'$ with the identity resolution of $I$. It is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so naturality of $\beta$, and then of its shifted version, gives the second equation by cancellation. Thus these are the specified resolution comparisons.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Section 07A5; derived.tex Tag 070I; resolution-comparison equations expanded here

proof.text:
Let $\Phi_{A,B}:\operatorname{Hom}(LA,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,RB)$ be the canonical derived adjunction $L\dashv R$. Apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to $G=v,F=u$, with $M=P,K=I$ and both denominator morphisms identities. The cone leg is $\alpha_P$, the cocone leg is $\beta_I$. These legs represent the essentially constant systems of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. For quasi-isomorphisms $t:P'\to M$ put $u_t=\alpha_{P'}L(Q_Yt)^{-1}$, a cone by naturality of $\alpha$; take $t_0:P_0\to M$ K-flat with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and $\rho=L(Q_Yt_0)\alpha_{P_0}^{-1}$, so $\rho u_{t_0}=1$. Given $t$, cofilteredness and a further such resolution give $t_k:P_k\to M$ with $P_k$ K-flat with flat terms and $a:P_k\to P_0$, $b:P_k\to P'$ over $M$; naturality of $\alpha$ and invertibility of $\alpha_{P_0},\alpha_{P_k}$ give $u_t\rho\,Q_Xv(a)=Q_Xv(b)$, the transition map. Dually $p_s=R(Q_Xs)^{-1}\beta_J$ for $s:I'\to J$ is a representing cocone, using a K-injective resolution [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. At identity indices the legs are $\alpha_P,\beta_I$. The cited pre-derived node's normalization formula says, for a homotopy map $g:P\to uI$, that $\Phi^{-1}(\beta_I Q_Yg)=Q_X(T^{-1}g)\alpha_P$. Taking $g=T(t)$ gives
$$\Phi_{Q_YP,Q_XI}(Q_X(t)\circ\alpha_P)=\beta_I\circ Q_Y(T(t)).\tag{*}$$
This formula covers every $a:LQ_YP\to Q_XI$: $a\alpha_P^{-1}$ has the form $Q_X(t)$ by the Hom bijection into K-injective $I$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], with $t:vP\to I$ a homotopy class. Invertibility of $\alpha_P$ is provided by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and of $\beta_I$ by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. No K-projectivity of $P$ or K-injectivity of $uI$ is used.

proof.text:
For $A=Q_YP$, $B=Q_XI$ and $a=Q_X(t)\alpha_P$, Step 3 gives $a[n]\ell_A=Q_X(t[n])\alpha_{P[n]}$. Formula $(*)$ for the shifted representatives, which are still in the resolution classes by Step 2, and $T(t[n])=T(t)[n]$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\Phi_{A[n],B[n]}(a[n]\ell_A)&=\beta_{I[n]}Q_Y(T(t[n]))\\
&=r_B^{-1}\beta_I[n]Q_Y(T(t))[n]\\
&=r_B^{-1}\bigl(\Phi_{A,B}(a)\bigr)[n].
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is precisely the right-hand comparison equation of Step 3. Every $a$ has the representation used here by Step 4, so this proves the displayed identity for all morphisms between these representatives.

source.place: Tag 0FND representative formula; explicit shifted calculation from Steps 1–4 (agent expansion)

proof.text:
Every $A\in D(R_Y)$ is isomorphic to $Q_YP$ for K-flat $P$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Every $B\in D(R_X)$ is isomorphic to $Q_XI$ for K-injective $I$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Choose $h:Q_YP\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $k:Q_XI\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. For $a:LA\to B$ put $a'=k^{-1}aL(h)$. Bifunctoriality of the adjunction gives $\Phi(a')=R(k^{-1})\Phi(a)h$. Naturality of $\ell$ gives $a'[n]\ell_{Q_YP}=k^{-1}[n](a[n]\ell_A)L(h[n])$; naturality of $r$ gives $r_{Q_XI}^{-1}R(k^{-1})[n]=R(k^{-1}[n])r_B^{-1}$. Substitute these into Step 5 and cancel the precomposition by $h[n]$ and postcomposition by $R(k^{-1}[n])$. Hence, for all $A,B,a$,
$$\Phi_{A[n],B[n]}(a[n]\ell_A)=r_B^{-1}\bigl(\Phi_{A,B}(a)\bigr)[n].\tag{**}$$
The only transport here is the displayed naturality equalities and cancellation of isomorphisms; it imposes no boundedness on either complex.

source.place: Tag 06YS and Section 07A5; derived.tex Tag 0DVC bifunctoriality; explicit isomorphism cancellation

proof.text:
In $(**)$ set $B=LA$ and $a=1_{LA}$. The definition of an adjunction Hom bijection gives $\Phi_{A,LA}(1)=\eta_A$ and $\Phi_{A[n],(LA)[n]}(\ell_A)=R(\ell_A)\eta_{A[n]}$. Thus
$$r_{LA}\circ R(\ell_A)\circ\eta_{A[n]}=\eta_A[n].$$
This is exactly compatibility with the unit as defined in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. The proof worked for each integer $n$, rather than only positive shifts.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; unit specialization of the explicit Hom calculation

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] (i) to the unit equality of Step 7. This gives, for every $B$,
$$\varepsilon_{B[n]}=\varepsilon_B[n]\circ\ell_{RB}\circ L(r_B).$$
Its clause (ii) gives uniqueness of $r$ for the fixed $\ell$, and identifies the inverse explicitly as
$$r_B^{-1}=R(\varepsilon_B[n])\circ R(\ell_{RB})\circ\eta_{(RB)[n]}.$$
The comparisons here are the canonical ones identified in Step 3. Existence of a compatible $r$ is Step 7, so for each $n$ the resolution comparison $r$ is the unique one compatible with the unit and $\ell$. This proves both shift compatibility clauses and the claimed uniqueness; no coherence of $\ell$ across different $n$ is used.
